Created by Bulgarian-born Slovak sculptor Emil Venkov, this statue was initially displayed in Poprad, Czechoslovak Socialist Republic (now Slovakia) in 1988, just a year before the Velvet Revolution.

In 1996, the owners moved the Statue of Lenin to a more prominent location at the intersection of Fremont Place North, North 36th Street, and Evanston Avenue North, where it remains today. Since its unveiling, the Statue of Lenin has become a local landmark, often adorned with decorations or subjected to vandalism.
